unit.why: Two short teaching-dialogues on memory (R. Elimelekh, R. Yitzhak Meir of Warsaw) lead into one small narrative: R. Moshe of Savran disputes a Talmudic citation with his dayan, proves himself right, and draws a moral from it.
unit.boundary_note: Opening sayings by R. Elimelekh and the Warsaw gaon are non-narrative; the story proper begins at 'וכעין זה שמענו'.

stories.start_quote: וכעין זה שמענו מהה״ק ר״מ מסאווראן ז״ל
stories.end_quote: ישנו בזכירה ואין שבחה לפניו והבן.
stories.summary_en: At a gathering R. Moshe of Savran quotes a Talmudic dictum, and his dayan R. Pinchas denies it is in the Talmud. The tsaddik, who had not studied that tractate for seventeen years, proves the dayan wrong. He then explains that one who guards himself from sin is free of forgetfulness.

quotes: מתי למדת מס׳ זו שידעת שלא נמצא
אני לא למדתי מס׳ זו זה בשבע עשרה שנה
tags.why: Study and recall of a Talmudic tractate is the plot

tags.why: The tsaddik closes with a homiletic exegesis
The anecdote sits inside a homiletic frame on memory and forgetting, with teachings before it and after it
